digest.component_or_area: rebar graph hierarchy resolver and dependency linking
propositions: A blocking-link resolver using TYPE_TIER for comparability decides incorrectly for siblings of different types, causing requested edges to go unrecorded while unintended ancestor-blocking edges are created instead.
Ancestor-blocking edges (where a ticket blocks its own ancestor or descendant) distort ready, next-batch, and parent-first cascade semantics, causing parallel agents to receive incorrect work orders.

Comparability for blocking links must be determined structurally by the parent hierarchy (nearest common ancestor) rather than by ticket type, and no blocking edge should be representable between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant.
Existing blocking edges written under the type-tier rule must be detectable and repairable store-wide in a single pass without breaking the escalation contract for callers.

The escalation behavior (auto-escalate cross-subtree links and emit redirect records) must remain unchanged for all existing callers including the link MCP tool and the reconciler's inbound apply path.
